items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Maya was nervous on the first day of school. She did not know anyone in her class. She sat down and the girl next to her said hi. By the end of the day, they were friends.

Retell the story and tell what the central message is.
items.answer: Maya was nervous on the first day of school because she did not know anyone. A girl said hi to her and by the end of the day they were friends. The central message is that a small kind act can start a friendship.

steps: Beginning: Maya was nervous. Middle: A girl said hi. End: They were friends. Message: A small kind act can lead to friendship.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sam did not want to clean his room. He put it off all day. At bedtime, his mom came in. She said he could not have a story until it was done. Sam cleaned his room fast. Then he got his story.

What lesson does Sam learn in this story?
items.answer: Sam learned that putting off chores just delays fun. It is better to do your responsibilities first.

steps: Sam avoided cleaning all day. This meant he could not have his story until he cleaned at the very end. If he had cleaned earlier, he could have had his story sooner. The lesson is that doing your responsibilities first makes things better.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Aisha found a wallet on the ground. It had money inside. She thought about keeping it. Then she took it to the school office. The office called the owner, who came to pick it up. The owner thanked Aisha.

Retell the story using beginning, middle, and end.
items.answer: At the beginning, Aisha found a wallet with money inside. In the middle, she thought about keeping it but took it to the office instead. At the end, the owner came to get it and thanked Aisha.

steps: Beginning: Aisha found a wallet. Middle: She turned it in even though she could have kept it. End: The owner got it back and thanked her.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo was the fastest runner in class. One day a new boy named Omar raced him. Omar won. Leo frowned. Then Leo shook Omar's hand and said, 'Good race.'

What does Leo's action at the end tell you about him?
items.answer: Leo was disappointed but showed good sportsmanship. He was a gracious loser who respected his opponent.

steps: Leo frowned, which shows he was upset. But then he shook Omar's hand and said 'Good race.' That is being a good sport. It tells us Leo is fair-minded even when he does not win.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Zoe saw her friend Ben sitting alone at lunch. She noticed he looked sad. She asked if she could sit with him. Ben smiled for the first time that day.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that noticing when someone is sad and reaching out to them can make a big difference.

steps: Zoe noticed Ben was sad and chose to sit with him. Ben smiled for the first time that day. One small act of kindness made a big difference for Ben. The message is about the power of noticing others and showing care.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Marco's little brother wanted to play with his toy truck. Marco said no and hid it under his bed. His brother cried. Marco felt bad. He got the truck and gave it to his brother. His brother stopped crying and smiled.

Retell the story and tell what the lesson is.
items.answer: Marco would not share his truck and his brother cried. Marco felt bad, so he got the truck and gave it to his brother, who smiled. The lesson is that sharing makes others happy and makes you feel good too.

steps: Beginning: Marco hid his truck. Middle: His brother cried and Marco felt bad. End: He shared the truck and his brother was happy. Lesson: Sharing brings happiness to everyone.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Ben bragged about how good he was at soccer. His team lost the big game because Ben tried to do everything himself instead of passing to his teammates.

What lesson should Ben learn from this experience?
items.answer: Ben should learn that working as a team is more important than trying to be the star alone.

steps: Ben bragged and tried to do it all himself. This led to his team losing. If he had passed to his teammates, they might have won. The lesson is that teamwork matters more than one person trying to be the hero.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Maya found a stray cat near her school. She brought it home and asked her parents if she could keep it. They said she had to show she was responsible first. Maya fed the cat every day and cleaned its space. Her parents said yes after two weeks.

Retell this story and tell what Maya learned about responsibility.
items.answer: Maya found a stray cat and wanted to keep it. Her parents wanted to see her be responsible, so she fed it and kept its space clean every day. After two weeks, her parents said she could keep it. Maya learned that responsibility means doing the hard work every day, not just when it is fun.

steps: Beginning: Maya found a cat and wanted to keep it. Middle: Her parents asked her to prove she was responsible. End: She did the work every day and earned the right to keep the cat. Lesson: Real responsibility means consistent effort.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Sam and Leo both wanted to be the line leader. They argued and pushed. Their teacher put them both at the back of the line. The next day, she picked someone else as line leader.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that arguing and pushing to get what you want can lead to losing the opportunity altogether.

steps: Both boys wanted the same thing and fought over it. As a result, neither got it. The next day someone else was chosen. The message is that fighting over something often means nobody wins, and that is a natural consequence of not handling disagreements well.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Aisha's family forgot her show and tell day. She had nothing to bring. She looked around the classroom and found a rock on the windowsill. She told the class three things she knew about rocks and everyone was impressed.

What does this story tell you about Aisha?
items.answer: Aisha is resourceful and creative. Instead of giving up when she had nothing prepared, she found a solution and made the best of the situation.

steps: Aisha had a problem but did not panic. She found what was available and used her knowledge to make it work. This shows she is quick-thinking and does not give up when things go wrong.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Leo told his friend Ben a secret. Ben told two other kids. Soon the whole class knew. Leo felt hurt. He stopped sharing things with Ben.

Retell the story and tell what lesson Ben should learn.
items.answer: Leo told Ben a secret. Ben told others, and soon everyone knew. Leo was hurt and stopped trusting Ben. Ben should learn that keeping a secret is part of being a trustworthy friend.

steps: Beginning: Leo shared a secret with Ben. Middle: Ben told others. End: Leo was hurt and did not trust Ben anymore. Lesson: A good friend keeps secrets and can be trusted.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Zoe always let her little sister have the first turn. One day, Zoe's sister ran ahead and took the best seat at the movie. She did not say thank you either. Zoe felt like being kind was not worth it.

Do you think Zoe should stop being kind? Use details from the story.
items.answer: Even though her sister was not grateful this time, one bad experience does not mean kindness is worthless. The story shows that kindness should not depend on getting thanks in return.

steps: Zoe felt like kindness was not worth it because her sister was ungrateful. But being kind is valuable even when it is not noticed. The story teaches that true kindness does not depend on being thanked.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Marco's class had a pet fish. One morning, Marco came in early and noticed the fish looked sick. He told his teacher right away. The teacher got help and the fish got better.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that speaking up when something is wrong can make a real difference.

steps: Marco noticed something was wrong and told someone. His quick action helped save the fish. If he had said nothing, the fish might not have survived. The message is about the importance of speaking up.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Ben practiced writing his letters every night. His handwriting was messy at first. After two weeks, his letters were neat and even. His teacher put his paper on the board.

Retell the story and tell what lesson it teaches about practice.
items.answer: At first Ben's handwriting was messy. He practiced every night for two weeks. By the end, his letters were neat and his teacher displayed his work. The story teaches that practice leads to improvement.

steps: Beginning: Messy handwriting. Middle: Daily practice for two weeks. End: Neat letters and recognition. Lesson: Practice improves your skills.

items.prompt:
Read the story below.

Maya wanted a puppy more than anything. She begged her parents every day. Her parents got tired of the begging. They said that if she asked one more time, the answer would always be no. Maya stopped asking and started doing extra chores instead. Her parents noticed. On her birthday, they surprised her with a puppy.

What is the central message of this story?
items.answer: The central message is that showing responsibility through actions is more effective than asking or begging.

steps: Begging did not work for Maya. When she stopped asking and started showing responsibility through chores, her parents took notice. Actions spoke louder than words. The lesson is that demonstrating you are ready is more powerful than just asking.
